newsitem.title: INDIA: Belgium says Russia should not fear NATO plan.
newsitem.headline: Belgium says Russia should not fear NATO plan.

text.p: Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke said on Monday NATO's plans to expand into eastern Europe were not directed against Russia.

The first Belgian foreign minister to visit New Delhi since 1981, Derycke told a news conference he was briefed about Russia's fears on NATO by Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral, who visited Moscow last week.
"I think it is necessary for a lot of reasons," Derycke said in response to a question whether NATO was still relevant after the end of the Cold War.
"There is a lot of instability, even in Europe," he said.
"The (NATO) construction is not against Russia," Derycke added. "We are for openness in the economic field with Russia, provided they clean up their own house first."
Gujral did not comment on Derycke's remarks, but Indian officials said New Delhi traditionally opposed expansion of military blocs.
"From that point of view we are closer to the Russian position against NATO's expansion," one foreign ministry official told Reuters.
U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Saturday she would unveil details of NATO's proposals for European security when she met Russian leaders later in the week.
Albright is focusing much of her 11-day trip to nine world capitals on NATO plans to expand into eastern Europe.
She plans to persuade Russia to agree by a NATO summit scheduled for July on a charter defining a special new relationship with the Western alliance.
